summary: Convenience wrapper that runs DOMPurify on jsdom for server-side use. Output matches DOMPurify, but it pulls 27 MB and 28 packages and inherits jsdom's exposure. Use only if you specifically need DOMPurify on the server.
reasoning: Same sanitization results as DOMPurify: 0 of 25 vectors executed.
Removes the need to wire jsdom yourself when you want identical behaviour on both sides.
Actively maintained wrapper: 10 releases in 90 days.
Zero advisories attributed to the wrapper itself.
caveats: 27.4 MB install and 28 packages, driven by jsdom. That is 16x sanitize-html and 28x xss.
Its vulnerability surface includes jsdom, not just DOMPurify.
Adds a second place to track advisories for the same sanitization outcome.
Single-maintainer wrapper around a project maintained by someone else.

evidence.label: Bypass test
evidence.detail: 0 of 25 vectors executed; identical output to browser DOMPurify.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: 2 direct dependencies (dompurify, jsdom), 28 installed packages, 27.4 MB install.

evidence.label: Throughput
evidence.detail: ~47-49 ops/s on a 60 KB document in Node, roughly 8x slower than sanitize-html.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: No wrapper-specific advisories; underlying DOMPurify 3.4.17 and jsdom are clean at review time.

evidence.label: Provenance
evidence.detail: No attestations on any version; manual publish.
